properties.name: St. Peter's Canal & Battery Park shore (Atlantic end)
properties.kind: canal banks (national historic site) and provincial park shore
properties.season_2026: DFO Maritimes tidal water: Atlantic mackerel Apr 1-Dec 31; striped bass open all year except Dec 30-31; groundfish (cod, pollock, winter flounder and, read conservatively, cunner and sculpin) only from the third Saturday in June to Labour Day (Jun 19-Sep 6, 2027 if the pattern repeats) - release them outside that window; rainbow smelt angling Aug 1-May 31 (closed Jun 1-Jul 31), dip net Apr 1-Jun 15 except Fridays to Sundays; American eel all year; sea-run trout Apr 15-Sep 30 (Sep 1-30: release every brook trout and use no natural bait for any trout). Historic Canals Regulations: no fishing within 10 m of the lock or approach wharves or from the bridge over the channel. The canal cut and St. Peter's Bay are treated here as ordinary tidal trout water (Apr 15-Sep 30), not Bras d'Or all-year water. Battery Provincial Park's 2026 season was Jun 5-Oct 19. 2026 rules; check the 2027 Anglers' Handbook and DFO notices before fishing.
properties.limits_2026: Mackerel 20/day; in 2026 no minimum size and one line with no more than 3 hooks (MAR-VAR-2025-071 and -102, both expire 2026-12-31); unless DFO renews them for 2027, the 26.8 cm minimum (nose to fork) returns; striped bass 1/day, 68-150 cm total length, release all others; groundfish 5/day in total, never keep halibut or northern/spotted wolffish; smelt 60/day (no more than 30 by dip net); eel 10/day, at least 35 cm; trout 5/day, 1 line/3 hooks, and no trout angling from 2 h after sunset to 2 h before sunrise.
properties.licence: None needed in tidal water; Battery Provincial Park's own page says fishing is permitted with a NS sport fishing licence, so carry a General licence if you fish from the park shore.
properties.access: Park in the lot at the south (St. Peter's Bay) end of the canal off Toulouse St (Parks Canada national historic site; grounds open year-round; Parks Canada lists daily visitor fees, youth free). Fish from the canal banks and from the Battery Provincial Park shore on the east bank, which runs south toward Jerome Point. Stay at least 23 m from the lock gates and more than 10 m from the approach wharves, off the Hwy 4 swing bridge, and give way to boats.
properties.tip: Fish the Atlantic end on an incoming tide at dawn or dusk with a string of small mackerel jigs or a shiny spoon. When the mackerel are thin, drop a small hook with clam or worm along the canal walls for cunner and flounder, and keep those only Jun 19-Sep 6.
properties.why: The village's classic shore spot, 4 min from St. Peter's on verified public land. Tourism listings invite visitors to fish the canal banks, a 2016 travel post saw mackerel anglers at the Atlantic end and called it a spring tradition, and an old forum thread lists the canal for mackerel. That is reputation, not catch data.
properties.caution: No angling from any bridge in Nova Scotia (MPFR s.15(a) with Schedule IV item 1; $200 ticket). No fishing within 23 m below any fishway, obstruction or leap (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)). Historic Canals Regulations s.7(e): never within 10 m of the lock or approach wharves, never from the swing bridge; this map also asks you to stay at least 23 m from the lock gates, because the tide reverses the flow in the cut and either side of the lock can be 'below' it (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)); magnet fishing is banned and there is no swimming within 40 m of a lock gate. Cunner, sculpin and winter flounder are legally groundfish: keep them only Jun 19-Sep 6, 2027 (if 2026 repeats), 5 in total, and release them outside that window. Mackerel are in DFO's Critical Zone: keep only what you will eat.

properties.name: St. Peter's Inlet shore (Bras d'Or end, Pepperell St)
properties.kind: roadside shore on the tidal Bras d'Or
properties.season_2026: Tidal Bras d'Or water; St. Peter's Inlet is not one of the handbook's Bras d'Or closed areas, so rainbow and brown trout are open all year with any gear except on Dec 30-31 (2026 order MAR-VAR-2026-022, in force to Dec 31, 2026; check the 2027 order), when all trout angling is closed. Smelt angling Aug 1-May 31, dip net Apr 1-Jun 15 except Fridays to Sundays; other species follow DFO Maritimes tidal rules. The province lists tidal Bras d'Or water among its winter fishing opportunities. 2026 rules; check the 2027 Anglers' Handbook and DFO notices before fishing.
properties.limits_2026: Bras d'Or rainbow/brown trout 5/day Apr-Sep and 2/day Oct 1-Mar 31, rainbows at least 35 cm; Bras d'Or brook trout follow the inland season, Apr 1-Sep 30, and none may be kept Sep 1-30, so release every brook trout from Sep 1 to Mar 31; 1 line/3 hooks and no trout angling from 2 h after sunset to 2 h before sunrise. Smelt 60/day (no more than 30 by dip net).
properties.licence: None needed for tidal species; carry a NS General Fishing Licence (age 16+) for Bras d'Or trout, because the handbook groups the Bras d'Or with inland trout waters.
properties.access: Pull fully onto the shoulder of Pepperell St (provincial road) about 0.8 km north-west of the canal, where the road runs about 10 m from the Inlet shore, and fish from the road allowance and the shoreline below it. Do not cross lawns or use private docks, and stay off the marina floats to the east.
properties.tip: In late fall and right after ice-out, cast a small spoon or a smelt-coloured streamer at first light; rainbows must be 35 cm to keep, so expect to release most. Smelt bite after dark on tiny hooks with a sliver of bait in Oct-Dec and again in Apr-May. In January-March fish only where open water reaches the shore, and never walk out on the Inlet ice.
properties.why: The nearest legal winter trout water to St. Peter's: the Inlet is tidal Bras d'Or, where rainbow and brown trout are open all year. The Bras d'Or produced a provincial-record 11.33 lb rainbow (2021), but the fishery once relied on fish escaping from aquaculture and nothing shows trout are plentiful, so treat it as a low-odds trophy option on a verified public road edge.
properties.caution: No angling from any bridge in Nova Scotia (MPFR s.15(a) with Schedule IV item 1; $200 ticket). No fishing within 23 m below any fishway, obstruction or leap (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)). Ice: stay off clear ice under 10 cm, treat white ice and any ice over current or tidal water as unsafe, and stop once the spring thaw starts. Release every brook trout from Sep 1 to Mar 31, and release any striped bass you are not keeping. Village street: never block driveways.

Most bass here will be under 68 cm and must be released.

properties.name: Johnstown Harbour shore (Johnstons Harbour Rd)
properties.kind: roadside shore on the tidal Bras d'Or
properties.season_2026: Tidal Bras d'Or water. Tidal Bras d'Or rainbow and brown trout are open all year with any gear except on Dec 30-31 (2026 order MAR-VAR-2026-022, in force to Dec 31, 2026; check the 2027 order), when all trout angling is closed, outside the handbook's listed closed areas. Mackerel Apr 1-Dec 31; smelt angling Aug 1-May 31; groundfish only from the third Saturday in June to Labour Day. 2026 rules; check the 2027 Anglers' Handbook and DFO notices before fishing.
properties.limits_2026: Bras d'Or rainbow/brown trout 5/day Apr-Sep and 2/day Oct 1-Mar 31, rainbows at least 35 cm; Bras d'Or brook trout follow the inland season, Apr 1-Sep 30, and none may be kept Sep 1-30, so release every brook trout from Sep 1 to Mar 31; 1 line/3 hooks and no trout angling from 2 h after sunset to 2 h before sunrise. Mackerel 20/day, 1 line/3 hooks (2026 orders MAR-VAR-2025-071/-102, no minimum size, both expire 2026-12-31; unless renewed, the 26.8 cm nose-to-fork minimum returns in 2027); smelt 60/day; groundfish 5/day in total in the summer window.
properties.licence: None needed for tidal species; carry a NS General Fishing Licence (age 16+) for Bras d'Or trout, because the handbook groups the Bras d'Or with inland trout waters.
properties.access: From Hwy 4 at Johnstown (26 min east of St. Peter's) take Johnstons Harbour Rd (provincial, one-lane gravel) where it runs along the water's edge of Johnstown Harbour. Park well onto the shoulder without blocking the lane and fish from the road allowance; do not use private wharves or cross yards.
properties.tip: Calm, sheltered Bras d'Or water: in May-June and again in October, cast small spoons or a streamer along the drop-offs at first light for rainbows (35 cm minimum); in July-August a string of small jigs can find mackerel.
properties.why: A quiet harbour road on the Bras d'Or shore, off the main highway. Bras d'Or trout and mackerel are documented lake-wide (DFO lists mackerel among the lake's recreational fisheries, and record rainbows come from the lake), but there is no site data.
properties.caution: No angling from any bridge in Nova Scotia (MPFR s.15(a) with Schedule IV item 1; $200 ticket). No fishing within 23 m below any fishway, obstruction or leap (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)). One-lane gravel road with little room: turn around only in public spaces. Chapel Island (Potlotek) reserve land lies about 5 km west along Hwy 4; do not fish or park on reserve shore. Release every brook trout from Sep 1 to Mar 31.

properties.name: Cranberry Lake (Oban Rd)
properties.season_2026: RFA 1 inland water (Cape Breton Island): trout Apr 1-Sep 30 (Sep 1-30: release every brook trout, no natural bait); white perch, brown bullhead and white sucker may be fished only while a trout season is open; smallmouth bass season = trout season. No inland angling at all when no sport-fish season is open. 2026 rules; check the 2027 Anglers' Handbook and DFO notices before fishing.
properties.limits_2026: Trout 5/day combined; white perch 10/day (new in 2026); brown bullhead 25; white sucker 25; keep every smallmouth bass and chain pickerel you catch; 1 line, no more than 3 hooks; no angling for sport fish (trout, smallmouth bass) from 2 h after sunset to 2 h before sunrise, and no angling of any kind in inland water from 22:00 to 06:00 (MPFR s.12(1) and s.12(3)); never use perch, bass, pickerel, bullhead, goldfish or crayfish as bait and never move live fish.
properties.licence: NS General Fishing Licence (age 16+). A 2026 licence covers Jan-Mar 2027 only; from Apr 1, 2027 buy the 2027 licence (Apr 1, 2027 to Mar 31, 2028). Licence-free days under the NS General Fishing Regulations s.10: Feb 13-15 and Jun 5-6, 2027. The February days do not help here: this water is closed to angling in winter.
properties.access: From St. Peter's take Oban Rd (provincial gravel road) north about 4 km and park on the shoulder where the road comes within about 12 m of the lake, beside its outlet. Verify on arrival: one map source puts the water farther from the road here, and if the road does not reach the shore, do not cross private land. The road allowance is assumed to run about 10 m each side of the road centreline (not surveyed): fish from the allowance and the water's edge below it. The strip beyond it is not confirmed public; Nova Scotia residents may walk uncultivated land under the Angling Act, but visitors should ask the owner, and nobody should cross posted, fenced or cultivated land.
properties.tip: Small, quiet lake: from ice-out in late April through June cast a small spinner or fish a worm under a bobber from 06:00 for brook trout, then switch to small jigs or worms for white perch on summer evenings before 22:00 (keep up to 10).
properties.why: A wild, unstocked lake 9 min from St. Peter's with very few buildings around it. The 1974 provincial survey recorded brook trout and white perch: presence only and 50 years old, so this is a scenic gamble rather than a proven numbers lake.
properties.caution: No angling from any bridge in Nova Scotia (MPFR s.15(a) with Schedule IV item 1; $200 ticket). No fishing within 23 m below any fishway, obstruction or leap (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)). Cranberry Lake's outlet brook leaves the lake about 17 m from the pin and passes under Oban Rd: fish the lake side of the road, never the brook below the road crossing (no fishing within 23 m below any obstruction). Fish the open lake, not stream mouths, which can carry different seasons. Never move live fish or dump bait; report new invasive fish to 902-485-5056. Wear hunter orange in the woods from mid-September to December (deer seasons, Sunday hunting allowed).

properties.access: From Port Hawkesbury take Kings Rd (provincial gravel road) to where it crosses Embrees Brook at the pond's outlet, about 7 m from the pond edge; park off the road and fish from the road allowance on the pond side. The road allowance is assumed to run about 10 m each side of the road centreline (not surveyed): fish from the allowance and the water's edge below it. The strip beyond it is not confirmed public; Nova Scotia residents may walk uncultivated land under the Angling Act, but visitors should ask the owner, and nobody should cross posted, fenced or cultivated land.
properties.tip: Restocked on June 2, 2026, so plan for early June: small spinners or a worm and bobber from shore.
properties.why: One of the few nearby waters on the drought-reduced 2026 stocking list, with 985 catchable, 35 large and 2,257 yearling brook trout in 2023-2025. A small (about 4 ha) put-and-take pond 22 min from Cleveland.
properties.caution: No angling from any bridge in Nova Scotia (MPFR s.15(a) with Schedule IV item 1; $200 ticket). No fishing within 23 m below any fishway, obstruction or leap (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)). Embrees Brook leaves the pond through a culvert under Kings Rd here: fish the pond on the pond side of the road, and do not fish the brook below the culvert. This pond is near the Port Hawkesbury protected watershed boundary, where fishing is banned except at MacIntyre Lake: obey any watershed sign. (MacIntyre Lake is not on this map: its approaches cross railway property.) Never move live fish or dump bait; report new invasive fish to 902-485-5056.

properties.name: River Denys Special Trout Management Area (Seal Cove, Denys Basin)
properties.kind: roadside basin shore (special trout management area)
properties.season_2026: River Denys Special Trout Management Area (River Denys, its tributaries, Denys Basin and Indian Pond, down to the Boom Channel line): closed to all angling Apr 1-30; trout May 1-Aug 31; Sep 1-30 release every brook trout and, to be safe, use no natural bait (the general September bait ban reaches STMAs; whether Denys Basin counts as the exempt Bras d'Or Lakes is unclear); closed to trout Oct 1-Mar 31 (the 2026 trout order MAR-VAR-2026-022 closes River Denys to trout Jan 1-Apr 30 and Oct 1-Dec 31). 2026 rules; check the 2027 Anglers' Handbook and DFO notices before fishing.
properties.limits_2026: 3 trout/day, only 1 longer than 35 cm; in September brown or rainbow only (3/day, 1 over 35 cm); 1 line/3 hooks; no trout angling from 2 h after sunset to 2 h before sunrise.
properties.licence: Carry a NS General Fishing Licence: the basin is tidal, but the handbook manages it with the inland and Bras d'Or trout waters.
properties.access: From Orangedale or the River Denys valley follow Marble Mountain Rd (provincial, paved) to the Seal Cove shore of Denys Basin, where the road runs about 10 m from the water about 85 m north-east of the Marble Mountain Rd bridge; park on the shoulder and fish from the road allowance and the shore below it.
properties.tip: May and June are the months: on a rising tide at dawn, fish a smelt-pattern streamer or a small spoon along the basin edge. Fish are often big but bites are few, so plan a morning, not an hour.
properties.why: The best-documented big sea-run brook trout fishery near Cleveland (42 min). The province tagged 341 sea-run trout here in 2008, and after a 2012 rule change the share of trout over 30 cm in anglers' catches rose from 47% to 70% (RFAC 2016; provincial data 2008-2016). A trophy fishery, not a numbers one; the pin is on the basin, well away from the river channel.
properties.caution: No angling from any bridge in Nova Scotia (MPFR s.15(a) with Schedule IV item 1; $200 ticket). No fishing within 23 m below any fishway, obstruction or leap (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)). River Denys is closed to salmon all year: fish the basin, never river pools, and release any salmon or kelt at once. Seal Cove Nature Reserve (about 800 m away) is closed to fishing. Closed to trout Oct 1-Mar 31 and to all angling in April. Stay at least 30 m from the Marble Mountain Rd bridge and never fish from it. MacKenzies Brook enters about 250 m away: fish the basin shore, not the brook mouth.

properties.name: Lake Ainslie east shore (Hwy 395)

properties.access: Park on the shoulder of Highway 395 on the east shore, about 52 min from Cleveland, and walk about 50 m west across Crown land to the lake.
properties.tip: Smallmouth bass hit soft-plastic grubs, tubes and small crankbaits along rocky drop-offs in July-August; keep and humanely kill every one. Mornings from 06:00 in late May-June are better for the stocked brook trout.
properties.why: This 5,700 ha lake holds an established smallmouth bass population (provincial catch rates rose from 2003 to 2008, and 2024 eDNA sampling found bass at most sites), plus white perch and yearly brook trout stocking (3,860 catchable and 225 large in 2023-2025). Keeping bass helps the Margaree's native fish.
properties.caution: No angling from any bridge in Nova Scotia (MPFR s.15(a) with Schedule IV item 1; $200 ticket). No fishing within 23 m below any fishway, obstruction or leap (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)). Lake Ainslie drains to the Margaree salmon system: release any salmon. Large, windy lake. Never move live fish or dump bait; report new invasive fish to 902-485-5056.

Salmon parr were released into Lake O'Law Brook, the outlet, in 2019-2020: fish the lake only, never the brook, and release any salmon, parr or small trout you cannot identify ('If you don't know, let it go'). An inlet brook enters about 100 m from the pin: fish the open lake, not the brook mouth. Middle River Wilderness Area adjoins the park (vehicles restricted). Never move live fish or dump bait; report new invasive fish to 902-485-5056.

properties.name: Gillis and Cameron lakes (Pinevale Rd)
properties.season_2026: RFA 2: Gillis and Cameron lakes are extended-season waters - trout open all year except Dec 30-31 (2026 order MAR-VAR-2026-022, in force to Dec 31, 2026; check the 2027 order), and white and yellow perch open all year; both are on the Jan 1-Mar 31 winter fishery list. 2026 rules; check the 2027 Anglers' Handbook and DFO notices before fishing.
properties.limits_2026: Trout 5/day Apr-Sep (September: natural bait is allowed here because this is an extended-season water; the handbook is unclear whether the September brook-trout release applies, so release brook trout in September to be safe), 2/day Oct 1-Mar 31; yellow perch 25/day; white perch 10/day; 1 line/3 hooks; no angling for sport fish (trout, smallmouth bass) from 2 h after sunset to 2 h before sunrise, and no angling of any kind in inland water from 22:00 to 06:00 (MPFR s.12(1) and s.12(3)).
properties.licence: NS General Fishing Licence (age 16+). A 2026 licence covers Jan-Mar 2027 only; from Apr 1, 2027 buy the 2027 licence (Apr 1, 2027 to Mar 31, 2028). Licence-free days under the NS General Fishing Regulations s.10: Feb 13-15 and Jun 5-6, 2027.
properties.access: From Hwy 104/Hwy 4 take Dunmore Rd about 10 km to Pinevale Rd (provincial gravel road) and follow it to Gillis Lake, where the road runs about 11 m from the shore; Cameron Lake is about 1.5 km further along the same road. About half of Gillis Lake's shore is Crown land. The road allowance is assumed to run about 10 m each side of the road centreline (not surveyed): fish from the allowance and the water's edge below it. The strip beyond it is not confirmed public; Nova Scotia residents may walk uncultivated land under the Angling Act, but visitors should ask the owner, and nobody should cross posted, fenced or cultivated land.
properties.tip: After the fall 'Winter Fishery' rainbow stocking (mid-September in 2025), fish small spoons or dough bait from shore in October-November, then through safe ice January-March; yellow perch take small jigs and worms year-round.
properties.why: Among the biggest catchable loads in the region: the records list up to 7,270 catchable and 400 large trout for Gillis and up to 6,254 and 425 for Cameron in 2023-2025, including 2,000 'Winter Fishery' rainbows each in September 2025, and both were stocked for the June 2026 derby. Nine Gillis and Cameron rows are identical in date, count and length, so some may record one combined release: do not add the two lakes together. No rainbows were raised in 2026, so winter 2026-27 will be thin; fall 2027 should recover if normal stocking resumes.
properties.caution: No angling from any bridge in Nova Scotia (MPFR s.15(a) with Schedule IV item 1; $200 ticket). No fishing within 23 m below any fishway, obstruction or leap (Fisheries Act s.34.3(4)(e)). Ice: stay off clear ice under 10 cm, treat white ice and any ice over current or tidal water as unsafe, and stop once the spring thaw starts. Narrow gravel road: park without blocking it. Busy after stocking and on derby days. Never move live fish or dump bait; report new invasive fish to 902-485-5056. South River Nature Reserve (about 3.5 km away) is closed to fishing.
